purpose: Review externally checkable claims with the right primary-source class before a draft page can be recommended for human verification or publication.
rules: Use SAP primary sources for SAP product behavior and release-sensitive statements.
Use the owning specification or standards body for protocol and interoperability claims.
Use original research for empirical or scientific claims where research evidence is material.
Keep documented facts separate from consultant heuristics, design guidance, and synthetic examples.
Author heuristics are allowed when clearly presented as judgement; they are not counted as source-supported facts.
Record product and release scope when the behavior can differ by deployment or release.
A source-supported claim is not the same as a human-verified page.
Do not change verified, robots, sitemap, or publication status from this review alone.
When primary sources disagree or scope is unclear, keep the claim in review and record the conflict instead of choosing the convenient answer.
Prefer a small set of load-bearing reviewed claims over a meaningless claim count.
promotion_boundary: This layer can prove that an externally checkable claim is supported by an appropriate primary source. It cannot declare the complete page verified or public.
